rows.jp: 霧の座席で食ってやるぞ。
rows.en: I was going to eat at Kiri's desk.

ghs.en: I'll just eat in Kiri's seat, yeah.

ghs.assessment: The narrator says that today's lunch was rice balls. 'Today we have' invents a plural subject and presents the meal rather than identifying what he brought or had.

highlights.text: Today we have rice balls.

rows.jp: ふりかけなどがまぜてあり、いかにもうまそうだ。
rows.en: They had seasoning mixed in and looked delicious.

ghs.en: There's furikake mixed in, and it looks really tasty.

ghs.assessment: いただきます is the conventional pre-meal expression. 'Thank you for the food' is a literalized explanation rather than a natural equivalent in this spoken context.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Thank you for the food."

rows.en: “...Why are you eating at my desk...?”
“It sure is. Why don't you sit down?”

ghs.assessment: The English dialogue opens a quotation mark but never closes it.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, right, that. Sorry.

rows.jp: 別の椅子を借りて座り直す。
rows.en: I borrowed another chair and sat down again.

ghs.en: I borrow another chair and sit back down.

rows.en: “Go on, eat. There's enough for two.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Gladden me with eating. There's enough for two."
ghs.assessment: 食べたまえ is a lightly grandiose command to eat. 'Gladden me with eating' invents a request to please the speaker and is not idiomatic English.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Gladden me with eating. There's enough for two."

ghs.en: Kiri: "...Miki's gone to procure some, so..."

rows.jp: 「つまむ程度かまわないだろ？」
rows.en: “Miki won’t mind if you just have a bite, will she?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You think she'd mind as long as it's snacking?"
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that Miki surely will not mind Kiri having just a bite. The English conditional construction is malformed and does not clearly state whose permission is at issue.

highlights.text: Taichi: "You think she'd mind as long as it's snacking?"

rows.jp: まあ、霧も弱気になっていたしな。
rows.en: Then again, Kiri had been feeling vulnerable lately.

ghs.en: Well, Kiri has lost heart too.

rows.jp: 「刃物とか武器になりそうなものには触れるなよ」
rows.en: “Don't touch any knives or anything else that could be used as a weapon.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Cutlery and that sort could be seen as weapon so hands off."
ghs.assessment: Taichi prohibits touching blades or anything else that could serve as a weapon. The English narrows this to cutlery, says it could merely be seen as a weapon, and is missing an article.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Cutlery and that sort could be seen as weapon so hands off."

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because I... don't want to die."

rows.jp: 「うむうむ。曜子ちゃんは強いからな。有言実行だし」
rows.en: “Good, good. Youko's strong—and when she says she'll do something, she does it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes-yes. Youko-chan's very powerful, see. And what she says she does."

rows.jp: 「……あの人は、どうしてあんな石投げがうまいんですか？」
rows.en: “...Why is she so good at throwing stones?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...how come that person is so skilled at stone throwing?"
Kiri: "That is weird, very much so."
ghs.assessment: ゼッタイ emphatically means 'definitely' or 'absolutely.' 'Very much so' is an unnatural degree phrase attached to 'weird.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "That is weird, very much so."

rows.jp: 「たいがいのことは上手だよ」
「根本的なデキが違うんだろう」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Her fundamental capacity of doing seems just different."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko is fundamentally made differently or has a different natural caliber. 'Her fundamental capacity of doing' is malformed and does not convey that comparison.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Her fundamental capacity of doing seems just different."

rows.jp: 何をやっても瞬時でコツを掴む。
rows.en: Whatever she tried, she got the hang of it instantly.

ghs.en: Whatever she does, she catches the trick in an instant.
ghs.assessment: コツを掴む means to get the knack or hang of something. 'Catches the trick' is a literal calque.

highlights.text: Whatever she does, she catches the trick in an instant.

rows.jp: 「特殊な訓練を受けてるとか？」
rows.en: “Did she undergo some kind of special training?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Did she get some special training?"

rows.jp: 「あー、受けてたね。なんか長期休みごとに、どっかの外国とか行って現地の軍事インストラクター雇って」
rows.en: “Oh, she did. Every long vacation, she’d go abroad somewhere and hire a local military instructor...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yep, she did indeed. Every lengthy vacation period she goes to some foreign country and hires a local military instructor."
ghs.assessment: Taichi describes what Youko used to do on each long vacation. The English switches the repeated past activity into the simple present.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Yep, she did indeed. Every lengthy vacation period she goes to some foreign country and hires a local military instructor."

ghs.en: She's at a loss for words.

rows.jp: 「投石もその時に習ったのかな。もしかしたら本物の羊飼いから習ったのかも」
rows.en: “Maybe that’s when she learned to sling stones. Or maybe she found an actual shepherd to teach her.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "She learned stone throwing in one of those occasions I guess. Might even be that she learned it from real-deal shepherds."
Taichi: "I am very glad of that."

rows.jp: 「他にもいろいろやってるはずだよ」
rows.en: “She must have trained in all sorts of other things too.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I expect there's been lots and lots of other stuff."

rows.jp: 「人生のほとんど自己の訓練に使ってる感じ」
rows.en: “Feels like she’s spent nearly her whole life training.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It feels like her life is almost entirely used for self-training."

rows.jp: 「俺もいっぱしの格闘家だけど、歯が立たないよ」
rows.en: “I’m a martial artist in my own right, and I still can’t touch her.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm a competent martial artist myself, but I couldn't hold a candle to her."

rows.jp: 「格闘なんてやってたんですか？」

ghs.en: Kiri: "What kind of martial art do you practice?"
ghs.assessment: Kiri asks in surprise whether Taichi practiced fighting at all. The English presupposes that he does and asks him to identify a discipline.

highlights.text: What kind of martial art do you practice?

rows.jp: よくぞ訊いてくれました。

ghs.en: How wonderful that I was asked!
Kiri: "Is it some plagiarism of Karate?"
Taichi: "You silly little brat you are WRONG!"

rows.jp: 「……あ、ごめん……ついカッとなって……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...ah, sorry... I just fired in a rage accidentally..."
ghs.assessment: カッとなって means that Taichi lost his temper in the heat of the moment. 'Fired in a rage accidentally' describes no intelligible English action.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...ah, sorry... I just fired in a rage accidentally..."

rows.jp: 霧は三メートルも逃げて、戦闘態勢を取っていた。
rows.en: Kiri had retreated ten feet and assumed a fighting stance.

ghs.en: Kiri escapes to three meters away, and went into combat readiness.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese narrates two coordinated past actions: Kiri retreated a full three meters and assumed a fighting stance. The English mixes present and past and uses the unidiomatic 'escapes to three meters away.'

highlights.text: Kiri escapes to three meters away, and went into combat readiness.

rows.jp: 「戻っておいで、食べたりしないから」
rows.en: “Come on back. I'm not going to eat you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Come back over here, I'm not gonna eat ya."
She returns, looking a touch anxious.

rows.jp: 「ささ、食べて食べて。優しい俺ですよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Come come, eat up eat up. It's the nice me now!"

rows.jp: 空手のパクりと言われると、我を忘れてしまう俺でもあった。
rows.en: Apparently, being told karade was a karate knockoff made me forget myself.

ghs.en: There is also a me that forgets hisself when he is called a Karate plagiarist.
ghs.assessment: The first-person narrator says that even he loses himself when accused of copying karate. The English shifts him into third person and uses the nonstandard reflexive 'hisself.'

highlights.text: There is also a me that forgets hisself when he is called a Karate plagiarist.

rows.jp: 「言わないけど、たぶん銃器も使える」
rows.en: “She hasn’t said so, but she can probably handle firearms too.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I can't really say, but maybe she can even use firearms."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that Youko does not talk about it but can probably use firearms. The English instead makes Taichi say that he cannot disclose the claim.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I can't really say, but maybe she can even use firearms."

rows.jp: 「格闘というか、組み討ちになったら一瞬で殺されるんじゃないかな。いろんなワザ持ってるし、こないだすごく高価なナイフ買ってたし」
rows.en: “If it came down to hand-to-hand combat—or grappling—she’d likely kill me in seconds. She knows all kinds of techniques, and the other day she bought an incredibly expensive knife.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "In hand-to-hand, if it comes to grappling, I think you might just get killed in an instant. She has knowledge of lots of techniques, and lately, she purchased this really expensive knife."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that he would probably be killed instantly if grappling with Youko. The English changes the endangered first-person speaker into a generic 'you.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "In hand-to-hand, if it comes to grappling, I think you might just get killed in an instant. She has knowledge of lots of techniques, and lately, she purchased this really expensive knife."

rows.jp: 「……そんな……いくらなんでも殺すなんて……」
rows.en: “...No... Surely she wouldn’t actually kill you...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...but then... no matter how you put it, it's all about the killing..."
ghs.assessment: Kiri protests that surely Youko would not actually kill someone. The English instead says that, however the matter is framed, it is all about killing.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...but then... no matter how you put it, it's all about the killing..."

rows.jp: 「自分だって俺のこと殺そうとしていたくせに」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Says the one who wanted to kill me herself."

rows.en: “Well, try not to dwell on it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Come now, it's nothing to worry about."
Kiri: "Senpai, you are... alright with it?"

rows.jp: 「わたし、あなたのこと……憎んでいます」

ghs.en: Kiri: "I, you, well... I detest you."

rows.jp: 「命を助けられて、何もできなくなった以上、こういう状況は仕方ありません」
rows.en: “You saved my life. I can’t do anything against you now, so... I suppose this is how it has to be.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "My life was saved, so I cannot do anything anymore, nor do anything to change this situation."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that because Taichi saved her life and she can no longer act against him, the present situation cannot be helped. The English turns the latter point into a vague inability to change the situation and obscures the causal sequence.

highlights.text: Kiri: "My life was saved, so I cannot do anything anymore, nor do anything to change this situation."

rows.jp: 「でも……あなたのことは変わらず嫌いです」
rows.en: “But... I still dislike you just as much as before.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "But... nothing changes, I still hate you."

rows.jp: 「そこは、勘違いしないでください」
「してないよ。それでいいと思うし」
rows.en: “I don't. And I think that's fine.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm not at all. I just think that's OK."

rows.jp: 「……でも、一緒にごはん食べて……馴れ合ってしまっては」
rows.en: “...But eating together like this... getting chummy with you...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...but, eating a meal together... trying to make friends..."
Taichi: "I just want to get a closer look, that's it."

ghs.assessment: Kiri accuses Taichi of teasing her. 'Mo-, mocker!' changes the accusation into an unnatural noun of address.

highlights.text: Kiri: "Mo-, mocker!"

rows.en: A faint blush rose to her cheeks.

ghs.en: She's just a bit red in the face.

rows.jp: 「宝石は触れて愛でるものじゃない」
rows.en: “You don't admire a jewel by putting your hands all over it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "A precious gem is not something to be admired by touching."
Taichi: "They're something to be enjoyed by looking."

rows.jp: 「……先輩には、確かにそんな部分があると思います」
rows.en: “...You really do have that side to you.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I think, Senpai, that there is certainly a part that acts like that in you."
ghs.assessment: Kiri says that Taichi certainly has such a side to him. 'A part that acts like that in you' is an ungrammatical calque.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...I think, Senpai, that there is certainly a part that acts like that in you."

rows.jp: 「気にくわないです。そんなに女の子で遊びたいんだったら、支倉先輩とそうしていればいいじゃないですか」
rows.en: “I don't like it. If you want to toy with girls so badly, go do it with Youko.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "It is something I cannot stomach. If you have to play around with girls like that, would it not be better for you to do so with Hasekura-senpai?"

rows.jp: 「わたしたちは、あなたのための娯楽道具じゃないんです」
rows.en: “We aren't playthings put here for your amusement.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "We... are not tools for the sake of your amusement."

rows.jp: 「だめ。彼女は自分を持ってない」
rows.en: “No. She has no will of her own.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Not happening. She can't hold herself down."
ghs.assessment: 自分を持ってない means that she has no self or identity of her own. 'Can't hold herself down' instead describes failed restraint.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Not happening. She can't hold herself down."

rows.jp: 「逃げてるんだよ。昔からそうだ」
rows.en: “She's been running away all her life.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I want to run away from her. Been like that for a long time."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that she is running away and always has. The English makes Taichi the one who wants to run away from her.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I want to run away from her. Been like that for a long time."

ghs.en: Taichi: "She just gets on my nerves."

rows.jp: 霧は意外なものを見る目つきを投げかけてきた。
rows.en: Kiri gave me a look of surprise.

ghs.en: Kiri threw a look at me that said she was discerning something unexpected.

rows.jp: 「……わたしには、先輩がたの関係が理解できません」
rows.en: “...I don't understand the relationship between you two.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...this relationship between you two, Senpai, is something I just cannot understand."

rows.jp: 「ま、あんま気にしちゃイヤン」
rows.en: “Well, don't you worry your pretty little head about it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, don'tcha worry too much about it."

rows.jp: 俺と曜子ちゃんのヒストリーは、楽しい思い出ではないのだ。何一つ。
rows.en: There wasn't a single happy memory in the history Youko and I shared.

ghs.en: In my history with Youko-chan there are no fun memories. Not a single one.

rows.jp: 「娯楽道具については、どうにもならんかな」
rows.en: “As for treating people like toys... I'm not sure I can do anything about that.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "As for amusement tools, I don't think there's much helping it."

rows.en: “...This is the best I can do.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...this is all that can be done."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that he is already doing the best he can. The English removes him as the agent and says only that this is all that can be done.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...this is all that can be done."

rows.jp: が適切な解説が構築されない。
rows.en: But no adequate explanation came together.

ghs.en: but I can't construct an appropriate explanation.

rows.jp: だいたい霧ちんは、だいたい俺を見抜いているのだから、ことさら説明する必要もない。
rows.en: Besides, Kiri-kins has more or less seen through me already. There is no particular need to explain.

ghs.en: Generally, Kiri-chin, well, she generally sees through me, so there's no need for particular explanations.

rows.jp: 「ああ。あと、できたら俺のそばにいた方がいいぞ」
rows.en: “Oh. And if you can, you should stay close to me.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yeah. Also, if you're able to stay close to me, that'd be best."

rows.jp: 「強く言ってあるから平気だと思うけど、俺が目を離してるときに霧ちんになにかする可能性もあるし」
rows.en: “I gave her a very stern warning, so you should be safe. But she might still try something while I'm not looking.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I told her firmly so I think we'll be alright, but there's the possibility that she'll do something should you get away from my sight, Kiri-chin."
ghs.assessment: The danger is what Youko might do to Kiri while Taichi takes his eyes off her. The English instead makes Kiri move out of his sight.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I told her firmly so I think we'll be alright, but there's the possibility that she'll do something should you get away from my sight, Kiri-chin."

rows.jp: 「俺にバレずに霧ちんをくびちょんぱしちゃうとかね」
rows.en: “She might snip your head right off without me ever finding out.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And without I becoming aware, poor Kiri-chin could get completely neckchopped."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that Youko might chop Kiri's head off without his noticing. The English uses a passive construction with the invented verb 'neckchopped' and loses the actor.

highlights.text: Taichi: "And without I becoming aware, poor Kiri-chin could get completely neckchopped."

ghs.assessment: がくがく describes Kiri trembling violently. 'With a clatter' wrongly presents the mimetic expression as an external sound.

highlights.text: Trembling with a clatter.

rows.jp: 「自分の命のため、俺のそばにいないといけない……ってことでいいじゃないか」
rows.en: “Just tell yourself you have to stay beside me for the sake of your life.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "For the sake of your life, thou must stay by my side... ain't that a nice thing to say?"
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that needing to stay beside him to protect her life is a perfectly good justification. The English changes this into 'a nice thing to say' and adds unsupported mock-archaic and eye-dialect speech.

highlights.text: Taichi: "For the sake of your life, thou must stay by my side... ain't that a nice thing to say?"

rows.jp: 「和解というか休戦って感じだな」
rows.en: “It isn't reconciliation so much as a truce.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Rather than reconciliation, this feels like armistice doesn't it."

rows.jp: 「そーいうわけで、今後は仲良く喧嘩しよう」
rows.en: “So from now on, let's fight like the best of friends.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And with that said, let's have our friendly squabbles from here on."

rows.jp: 不承不承、霧は右手を……出すが握手が出来ない。
rows.en: Reluctantly, Kiri offered her right—and discovered that we couldn't shake hands that way.

ghs.en: Unwillingly and grudgingly, Kiri puts out her right hand and... cannot shake hands.

rows.jp: むっとして、手を引っ込める。
rows.en: She scowled and pulled it back.

ghs.en: Kiri: "......you are making me look stupid!"
ghs.assessment: 馬鹿にする means to make fun of or treat someone like a fool. 'Making me look stupid' instead means causing other people to view her badly.

highlights.text: Kiri: "......you are making me look stupid!"

rows.jp: 「だから冗談にいちいち怒らないでくれ」
rows.en: “That's why you need to stop getting angry at every little joke.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm telling you, don't just get angry at every single joke!"

rows.jp: ちゃんと右手を出しなおし、霧の右手を握る。
rows.en: This time I offered my right hand properly and took hers.

ghs.en: I correct and extend my right hand, and shake Kiri's right hand.

rows.jp: 確かに武器なんて似合わない。
rows.en: Weapons truly do not suit it.

ghs.en: Certainly it's not suited for weapons.

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんという危険な橋を経て、少し関係が改善されたようだ。
rows.en: By crossing the dangerous bridge that is Youko, our relationship seems to have improved a little.

ghs.en: Passing through the dangerous bridge that is Youko-chan, our relations have improved just a bit.

rows.jp: 「じゃあ休戦調停を祝っておむすびパーティーだ」
rows.en: “Then let's celebrate our negotiated truce with a rice-ball party.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Then, this is a rice ball party to celebrate the settlement of an armistice!"

rows.jp: 「……こわいお人だ……敵さえも味方に……」
rows.en: “...A terrifying man... winning over even his enemies...”

ghs.en: Miki: "...scary guy him... even enemies he makes allies..."
ghs.assessment: Miki calls him a frightening man who even turns enemies into allies. The English is a string of malformed fragments with unstable pronouns.

highlights.text: Miki: "...scary guy him... even enemies he makes allies..."

rows.en: “This is my legendary Three Visits to recruit Zhuge Liang.”

ghs.assessment: 三顧の礼 invokes an elaborate, repeated, respectful solicitation. 'I just asked very politely' discards both the allusive force and the exaggeration.

highlights.text: Taichi: "I just asked very politely."

ghs.assessment: Kiri's elliptical 違う rejects his account as wrong. The isolated past-tense 'didn't' has no subject or complement.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...didn't..."

rows.jp: 「あー、なんか食べてるー、この大量の食料はどうするのー？」
rows.en: “Hey! Somebody's already eating! What am I supposed to do with all this food?”

ghs.en: Miki: "Ahhh, why are you even eeeating, what will we do with this huge bag of foood?"
ghs.assessment: Miki asks why they have already started eating and what she is to do with all the food she brought. 'Why are you even eating' changes the temporal complaint and is grammatically awkward.

highlights.text: Miki: "Ahhh, why are you even eeeating, what will we do with this huge bag of foood?"

rows.jp: 美希はトートバックの中身を、どさどさと机に落とした。
rows.en: Miki dumped the contents of her tote bag onto the desk.

ghs.en: Miki let the contents of her tote bag fall, paf-paf-paf in rapid succession, on top of the desk.

rows.jp: 山になって机から溢れた。
rows.en: The pile grew until it spilled over the edges.

ghs.en: It became a mountain that spilled off the edge.
Kiri: "...where's canned food and the rest?"

rows.jp: 「うーむ。お菓子を昼飯がわりにするのは……つらそうだ」
rows.en: “Hmm. A lunch made entirely of snacks sounds... rough.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Uh-huh. Using junk food in the stead of a proper lunch... that looks nasty."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that substituting snacks for lunch looks difficult or unpleasant. 'Looks nasty' suggests disgust, and 'in the stead' is malformed in this construction.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Uh-huh. Using junk food in the stead of a proper lunch... that looks nasty."

ghs.assessment: The ordinary expression is 'bad for your health.' 'Bad for the health' uses an unsupported definite article.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Terrible for the health, too."

rows.jp: 「でも美希はお菓子が大好き」
「わたしも、もうおなかいっぱいだから」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Me too, but my stomach's full, so..."

rows.jp: 「じゃあ一人で食べますもん」

ghs.en: Miki: "Well then, I'll eat them alone!"

ghs.assessment: The Japanese narrates that Miki sulked. 'Sullen' is an adjective fragment and does not state the action or change of state.

highlights.text: Sullen.

rows.en: “Miki loves snacks even if she gets fat.”

highlights.text: Miki: "I'll still fatteningly love sweets!"

rows.jp: ポテトチップを食べ出す。

ghs.en: She sets out to eat potato chips.

rows.jp: 「内心気にしてるんじゃないか」

highlights.text: Taichi: "But inside yourself this annoys you, doesn't it?"

rows.jp: 「ほれ、じゃあこの握り飯をやろう」
rows.en: “Here. You can have this rice ball.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "C'mon, I'll give you this onigiri!"

rows.jp: 成人男性サイズになっているから、美希ちんにはちょうどいいだろう。
rows.en: It was man-sized, which made it just right for Miki-kins.

ghs.en: Because it's been made to adult male size, it should be just fine for Miki-chin.

rows.jp: 俺が多少物足りないが……まあいいか。
rows.en: It would leave me a little hungry... but that was fine.

ghs.en: It's not that much for me, but... ah, it's fine.

ghs.assessment: 手料理 means homemade food or cooking. 'Handmade cooking' is an unnatural literal compound.

highlights.text: Miki: "Aaah, it's handmade coooo～king!"

rows.jp: ひし、とおにぎりを持った手にすがりつく。
rows.en: She latched onto the hand holding the rice ball.

ghs.en: Hug!, she clings to the hand that's holding the onigiri.
ghs.assessment: The mimetic ひし conveys that Miki clings tightly. The inserted exclamation 'Hug!' names a different action.

highlights.text: Hug!, she clings to the hand that's holding the onigiri.

rows.jp: はみはみと食べ始める。

ghs.en: Chomp chomp she sets to eat,

rows.jp: お菓子の山が残される。
rows.en: The mountain of snacks was still there.

ghs.en: while the mountain of sweets is left untouched.

rows.jp: 「……女の子なのに不安な食生活だな。いつもこうなの？」
rows.en: “...That’s a worrying diet for two girls. Do you always eat like this?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...for being girls your eating habits seem unstable. Is it always like this?"
ghs.assessment: Taichi calls their diet worrying or precarious. 'Eating habits seem unstable' is an unnatural collocation and does not convey his concern cleanly.

highlights.text: Taichi: "...for being girls your eating habits seem unstable. Is it always like this?"

ghs.en: Kiri: "Sometimes it's canned food, sometimes it's bread."

rows.jp: 「ほれ、トマトだ。ちょうど二つある」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Here, tomatoes. Just two of them."

rows.jp: 「…………やっぱりこの人は……いじめっこだ」
rows.en: “...I knew it. This man is a bully.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "......I knew it, this guy's... just a bully."

ghs.assessment: Miki says that she feels as though she is about to cry. 'Feels I'm crying' is malformed and changes an imminent reaction into an ongoing one.

highlights.text: Miki: "Feels I'm crying!"

ghs.assessment: Kiri says that being alive is good. 'Living it up' instead means enjoying oneself extravagantly and loses the statement about life itself.

highlights.text: We're living it up here.

rows.jp: どんな食生活だったんだ、この二人。
rows.en: What had these two been living on?

ghs.en: What kind of eating habits do these two even have...

rows.jp: 美希と霧が、口を『＊』状にしながらトマトを食べる様を横目に見ながら、俺は水筒で喉を潤した。
rows.en: I took a drink from my canteen, glancing at Miki and Kiri as they ate their tomatoes, mouths puckered into little asterisks.

ghs.en: While looking sidelong at Miki and Kiri's mouths go 『＊』-shaped via tomato eating, I quench my thirst with my canteen.
ghs.assessment: The narrator watches the two eat with puckered mouths while taking a drink. 'Mouths go ... via tomato eating' is a calque, and the sentence inconsistently switches to present tense.

highlights.text: While looking sidelong at Miki and Kiri's mouths go 『＊』-shaped via tomato eating, I quench my thirst with my canteen.

rows.jp: じっくり見られちゃってる！！
rows.en: She’s giving us a good long look!

ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that she is giving them a long, intent look. 'We're being calmly looked at' is unidiomatic and misreads じっくり as calmness.

highlights.text: We're being calmly looked aaat!!!

ghs.en: She's just a big clump of jealousy isn't she...

rows.jp: 俺に気取られるように姿を見せているってことは……当てつけなんだろうな。
rows.en: If she is showing herself where I can notice her... she must be doing it out of spite.

ghs.en: Her showing herself to me is the same as suspecting me... this is an insinuation.
ghs.assessment: Taichi infers that Youko is deliberately showing herself where he can notice as a spiteful display directed at him. The English instead introduces suspicion and an insinuation.

highlights.text: is the same as suspecting me... this is an insinuation

rows.jp: くのいちだから本来隠密度高いし。
rows.en: She is a ninja. Stealth is normally her specialty.

ghs.en: Being a Kunoichi, she has a high level of inherent stealthiness,

rows.jp: 俺なんかに見つかる彼女ではないのだ。
rows.en: She would never let someone like me spot her.

ghs.en: so this isn't me having spotted her, not at all.

rows.jp: 「……俺たちは市原式諜報術で監視されているのだ」
rows.en: “...We're under surveillance by the Ichihara School of Housekeeper Espionage.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...we are being monitored with the Intelligence Techniques of the Ichihara Style."

rows.jp: 「Ｅ・市原を頂点とする、凄腕くのいち集団が伝えるスパイ技術だ」
rows.en: “Spycraft passed down by an elite sisterhood of housekeeper-ninjas, headed by E. Ichihara.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "A spy technique imparted by a group of resourceful Kunoichi, led by E. Ichihara."

rows.en: Kiri must have seen her too.

ghs.assessment: The line means that Kiri seems to have spotted her too. 'Seems Kiri has seen' omits the object and the necessary complementizer.

highlights.text: Seems Kiri has seen.

rows.jp: 「先輩っ、せっ、せんぱ……あ、あれあれ……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Senpai! Se-, Senpa--- it-, it's it's..."

rows.jp: 「平気だ、俺のそばにいるんだ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "You're fine, you're by my side."
ghs.assessment: Taichi reassures Kiri and tells her to stay by his side. The English changes the instruction into a statement that she is already beside him.

highlights.text: you're by my side

rows.jp: 霧が指さす。美希が「んに？」と見る。

ghs.en: Kiri points. Miki looks with a 'what?'.

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんの姿はない。
rows.en: Youko was nowhere to be seen.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Youko is no longer there. 'Her figure is not there' is a literal and unnatural way to report her absence.

highlights.text: Youko-chan's figure is not there.

rows.jp: 「……え？　なにもないけど、どったの？」

ghs.assessment: どったの is a casual 'what's wrong?' The invented contraction 'whass'it?' instead asks what an object is.

highlights.text: Miki: "...eh? There's nothing there, whass'it?"

rows.en: “B-but she was there just now... Taichi?”

ghs.en: Kiri: "N-, now, I'm sure that... Senpai?"

rows.jp: 「志村現象だ。美希にはもはや物理的に曜子ちゃんを観測することはできない」
rows.en: “The Shimura ‘Behind You!’ Phenomenon. Miki is now physically incapable of observing Youko.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's the Shimura Feno--- Phenomenon. Miki is no longer physically capable of observing Youko-chan."

rows.jp: 太一物理学。安定している特定状況内で発生する観測問題の一種。見る者は見るが、見えない者は見えないまま属性が固定され、それが物理的に反映される。状況内で大きな変化があると属性は破棄されることが多い。
rows.en: Taichi Physics. A class of observer problem that occurs within certain stable situations. Those who can see, see; those who cannot remain unable to see, and the assigned property manifests physically. A major change in the situation will usually clear the property.

ghs.en:
* Shimura Phenomenon---
Taichian Physics. A type of observational problem
that occurs within specific, stable situations.
The observer looks, but the unseen subject has
its Still Unseen Attribute fixed, which reflects
on the physical world. Frequently, a drastic
change in the situation causes this attribute
to be lost.

rows.jp: 霧は死ぬほど緊張していた。

rows.en: I put an arm around her shoulders on instinct.

ghs.assessment: Taichi reflexively puts an arm around Kiri's shoulders. 'Hold her shoulders' suggests gripping them with his hands rather than the enclosing gesture.

highlights.text: Reflexively I hold her shoulders.

rows.jp: ひく、と曜子ちゃんの目尻が震えた。
rows.en: The corner of Youko's eye twitched.

ghs.en: Twitch, and the corner of Youko-chan's eye quivered.

rows.jp: これは滅茶苦茶珍しいことです。
rows.en: This is an extraordinarily rare occurrence.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese calls the reaction extraordinarily rare. 'Unreasonably rare' wrongly evaluates the rarity as irrational.

highlights.text: That is something unreasonably rare.

rows.jp: 霧は緊張していて、俺の慣れなれしさには気づかない。
rows.en: Kiri was too tense to notice how familiar I was being.

ghs.en: Kiri is so tense, she doesn't even notice my overfamiliarity,

rows.jp: 切羽詰まった猫みたいだ。

ghs.en: like a cornered cat at its wits' end.

rows.jp: 愛おしい反面と、壊してしまいたいという欲求。
rows.en: Affection for her—and the urge to break her.

ghs.en: Lovability on one side, on the other, the want to destroy.
ghs.assessment: The narrator feels tenderness or affection on one side and an urge to destroy on the other. 'Lovability' describes a quality in Kiri rather than his feeling toward her.

highlights.text: Lovability on one side, on the other, the want to destroy.

rows.jp: 二つは同時に存在していた。
rows.en: Both existed inside me at once.

ghs.assessment: 気をつけろ warns Kiri to be careful or watch out. 'Pay attention' suggests attending to information rather than danger.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Kiri-chin, pay attention!"

rows.jp: 「危害はないとしても、嫌がらせをしてくる可能性がある」
rows.en: “Even if she doesn't hurt you, she might resort to harassment.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Even if harm doesn't come, there is still the possibility of harassment."
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that even if Youko does not physically harm Kiri, she may harass her. The English removes both actor and target and uses the unnatural phrase 'harm doesn't come.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Even if harm doesn't come, there is still the possibility of harassment."

rows.jp: 「い、嫌がらせ？　具体的にはどうなんです？」
rows.en: “H-harass me? What exactly would she do?”

rows.jp: 「えーと……かなり陰湿だと思うよ」
rows.en: “Well... I imagine she’d do something pretty underhanded.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Uhmmm... something fairly malicious, of the wet and private kind I think."
ghs.assessment: 陰湿 means insidious, underhanded, or malicious. The English invents 'of the wet and private kind,' which has no support in the Japanese.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Uhmmm... something fairly malicious, of the wet and private kind I think."

rows.jp: 「尊厳を奪ったり、シャレで済まないギリギリのところで辱めたり」
rows.en: “Strip away your dignity. Humiliate you right to the point where no one could laugh it off.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Forcible deprivation of dignity perhaps, humiliating you and then brushing it off as a joke at the very last instant."

rows.jp: 「……あなたと一緒じゃないですか」

ghs.en: Kiri: "...is that that not the same as what you do?"
ghs.assessment: The English repeats 'that' and produces a malformed question.

highlights.text: Kiri: "...is that that not the same as what you do?"

rows.en: “...I knew it... I can't trust you.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...I knew it... you can't be trusted."

rows.jp: 霧は美希のそばに戻っていった。
あああ、同性に寝取られた。
rows.en: Aaaah. Another woman had stolen my girl.

ghs.assessment: The Japanese makes a comic remark about being romantically supplanted by someone of the same sex. Turning the noun into the nonce verb 'netorare'd' leaves the idea untranslated.

highlights.text: Ahhhh, same-sex netorare'd!

rows.en: I decided to resent Miki for it.

ghs.en: I attempt to bear a grudge against Miki.
